Okay, now that I've finally had a chance to manage to get some items off of my plate, I finally managed to test out my "Challenge" game as listed below:

Target Practice, or "More Dakka!"

Heroes:  Chrono Ranger, Expatriette, Bunker, Wraith and Tempest

Villain:  Grand Warlord Voss (alternatively, Citizen Dawn, The Dreamer, The Chairman, or any other high-minion villain will do.  I tend to avoid ones with equipment destruction, as that really hurts the whole field and can make the challenge un-fun)

Environment:  The Final Wasteland (alternatively, any other environment with a many environment targets, such as Silver Gulch or Insula Primalis)

Scenario:  Determined to find out once and for all who's the best shot, Jim, Expatriette, Bunker, and Wrath suit up and head into the training room for some target practice.  Wraith asks Tempest to act as an impartial third party, keeping score and ensuring that everyone stays safe.  

Additional Rules:  Tempest begins the game with a copy of Otherwordly Resilience and Cleansing Downpour in play, but only begins the game with 3 cards in hand.  Tempest may not deal damage to any Environment or Villain Target aside from the Villain himself.  If Tempest would deal damage to another Environment/Villain Target, that damage is reduced to 0.  Tempest may destroy or remove such targets (such as through "Into the Stratosphere"), though he may not actually deal damage or receive points for doing so.

Each time a hero destroys a Villain or Environment target, they receive a number of points as listed on the chart below.  The hero with the most points is declared Best Marksman.  If a hero is incapacitated over the course of the game, they lose all of their points immediately.

Point Values:

Starting Target HP            Point Value

>4                                       1

4-7                                      2

8-12                                    3

13+                                     4

Main Villain                         5

Sefirit:

 

How does this work if a villian target has say 12 HP and one hero does 10 damage to it on their turn and then next hero in line finishes it off with a measly 2 point shot?

 

Points are always based on the target's starting HP, and awarded to whomever destroys/kills/removes the target.

So, if Chrono Ranger takes the Stalwart down from 15 to 4 HP, and Bunker finishes it off, Bunker gets 3 points and CR gets none.

Since we had a few posts in this thread where people talked about how amazing Expat was I figured I would share my experience in a game I just finished playing.  The set up was

Kismet, AA, Expat, AZ, TLT, DV in Silver Gultch.  Now consider the help TLT gives.  I wish I had recorded the number of turns but she let everyone draw and extra card every single turn from her power plus played the card that lets everyone draw a card 3 times so everyone is looking at 3+rounds extra cards in their hand.

Despite this Expat didn't have a gun out until turn 4 when she played an arsenal access to choose between an SMG or flak jacket.  She didn't get another gun out the entire game. 

She did have hair trigger out fairly early but only used it on 3 turns (though it should have been 5 if you count flipping talismans).  Over the course of the game her best turn was when she put hollow points on the smg and hit 3 targets for a total of 3 damage each.  In the entire game she did 24 damage, 3 from hair trigger, 4 using an RPG to kill an eviroment card, 9 on the turn descirbed, 6 on a turn with hollow points and two targets, and 2 on a turn where she hit two targets for 1 damage each.  Some of this damage was even unwanted as she was hitting the talisman when we didn't necessarily want to.   Total damage to Kismet, a whopping 9 damage.

Half they game she couldn't attack, the other half she could barely attack AND THAT IS WITH ALL THE EXTRA CARD DRAW FROM TLT.  Now to be fair I guess she out damaged both AA and DV, but come on, thats not their game and she doesn't do anything else.  That was a frustrating game and exactly the point.  This is the third time I've seen this situation with her.  This is why people think arsenal access needs to be a search or she needs some extra card draw or something.  It happens, it happens too often, and when it does its not just a little suck, its a lot of suck.

Does your team appreciate it when you spend two rounds doing nothing while a Visionary player allows for card accelleration each turn?  I'm just curious, because my group generally is disappointed (and, to be quite frank, bored) when anyone has to spend multiple turns exclusively drawing cards to get what they need.  And I think that's the point.  WHY do we need to spend so many turns waiting with Expatriette?  If we're talking about how fun she is, is it really an incredibly titilating experience waiting and waiting to draw the card you want?  Again, it's that lack of card draw and her spotty search cards that make her boring games all the more painful.  Every other hero has multiple cards with "Draw a card" or one to many "Search your deck..." cards.  Expat just doesn't and I really don't know why.  I don't know why she has an Arsenal with nothing but Incendiary Rounds and a Flak Jacket when all I really need is an Assault Rifle.  It's mechanically and thematically unsatisfying.  I've had incredible games with The Visionary and I've had terrible ones.  Even when I'm getting the snot kicked out of me, I generally feel heroic as The Visionary, because I generally have what I need to help the heroes save the day with her plethora of card draw.

If she isn't your thing, I get it, but if you're saying that Expatriette is a more fun experience due to skipping multiple rounds to find the card you need rather than helping your teammates out with some card accelleration and deck manipulation as The Visionary, I really don't get it.  In one instance, you're contributing nothing to the team and doing nothing for entire rounds of gameplay (which sounds incredibly boring), and in the other you're consistently and meaninfully contributing to the field (or using her card accelleration to get something useful, which actually involves the player actively participating in the game).  If anything, when Expat is without cards and without options, I feel boring and worthless.  With a bad Visionary hand, it's just boring.

Also, Abs has OMI (card draw and search) Glacial Structure (card draw), Modular Realignment (trash recovery), so (thought I have had plenty a frustrating game with him) he has the potential to actually recover on his own from a poor hand.

Flamethrower, as always, has a strong grasp of the game and the criticisms levied for and against the heroes.  Generally Legs Galvanizing alone helps turn the tides, and Scholar has so much card accelleration and deck search that it's almost funny when he can't get what he needs.

If you read what I wrote, it should be obvious that when I said "bombing out" I meant that she manages to lose a single game, not that she never wins. I'm using 74.5%  as the benchmark, because that's the median win rate; I don't really understand why you'd use anything else. Wraith was a bit of a curiosity, but the jump is tempered a bit by the fact that you got a ton of new data in the last month (at least doubled, IIRC). A 1.4-sigma deviation is a lot more common than 2-sigma, and with the number of heroes we have, someone moving like that is expected. I will say that I think she is better than the stats indicate, though. Maybe the same is true of Expat.

 

As for any character being so bad they aren't worth playing ... someone has to be on the bottom, and there isn't really any good reason for it not to be Expat, Fixer, Bunker and AZ. And yes, I have won my share of games with Bunker and AZ, so their stats have never bothered me. I do wonder, though, whether it's just that these are the toughest heroes to play correctly. I could definitely stand to be better with Bunker.

 

And now for the last bit, I didn't see anyone say that Expat is so bad that she's broken and not worth playing. What I mostly see are people saying that her deck doesn't work the way it's supposed to more often than it should, and when that happens it's really unfun.
